record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Dynamics of the Expression of Gene Interaction Networks
record.original_question: Assume the gene-interaction rule A is context-dependent, so that the effect of one molecule or gene on another is influenced by the presence of additional molecules, and therefore A is a nonlinear function of the expression levels of two or more genes x_j, with j = 1, 2, ..., q and q ≥ 2. Given experimentally observed attractor data x_f, and possibly limited intermediate observations x_n, what properties of this unknown multi-gene nonlinear interaction rule A can be determined when the biological interactions depend jointly on multiple gene-expression levels rather than on each gene separately?

evidence.quote: 3) Open Problem III. Determine A where A is a Nonlinear Function of the Gene Expression of Multiple Genes.

Experimental evidence demonstrates that biology is often "context dependent", namely, that the effect produced by the binding of any one molecule A on molecule B is influenced by the presence of a third molecule C. For example, the effect of the binding of transcription factors on the regulatory region of a gene is influenced by the other transcription factors already bound at nearby sites on the DNA, see [Barash et al.,, 2003], In this case A is a nonlinear function of two or more of the gene expression levels, x_j, j = 1, 2, ...q, q ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a system of q ≥ 2 genes whose expression levels at time t are described by a vector x(t) = (x_1(t), …, x_q(t)) ∈ R^q evolving according to a dynamical rule of the form dx/dt = A(x), where A : R^q → R^q is an unknown nonlinear interaction function that is context-dependent: the influence of one component on another depends jointly on the values of two or more components rather than on each component separately (so A cannot be decomposed as a sum of single-variable contributions). Suppose one is given experimental data consisting of (i) one or more observed attractor states x_f of the dynamics (fixed points or limit cycles of A), and (ii) possibly a limited collection of intermediate state observations {x_n} sampled along trajectories.\n\nProblem: Determine which qualitative and quantitative properties of the unknown multi-gene nonlinear interaction rule A can be reconstructed from such data. In particular, identify conditions on the observation set {x_f, x_n} under which the structure of A (for example, its dependencies, monotonicity patterns, joint nonlinear couplings between groups of variables, or its functional form up to a specified class) can be uniquely recovered, and characterize the obstructions to identifiability when the data are limited to attractors together with a sparse set of intermediate observations.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction concerning identifiability of context-dependent nonlinear gene interaction rules from attractor and limited trajectory data. No specific resolution was located; related work on network inference and identifiability addresses special cases but not the general formulation stated here.
